metadata.case_name: WONG WOON HEI v. DICKSON CONSTRUCTION CO., LTD. AND OTHERS

plaintiff.occupation_after: watchman, shop assistant or car park attendant

source: the plaintiff suffered a fracture of the left calcaneum.

manifestations.description: he now has pain and swelling in the left ankle
every step he takes is painful
He has to walk with a stick
the ankle is not strong enough to support him when he has to squat over a lavatory basin
restricted dorsiflexion and plantarflexion of the left foot
restricted inversion and eversion to less than five degrees
some muscle wasting in the left leg
pain in the sub-talar joint during weight bearing

treatments_received: removal of the surgical implant from his left ankle
physiotherapy (twice weekly from October 1997 to October 1998)
out-patient treatment at the specialist clinic of Queen Mary Hospital (November 1997 to January 1999)
transfer to the Maclehose Medical Rehabilitation Centre (1 April 1999 to 2 July 1999)

losses.description: he now has pain and swelling in the left ankle, and that every step he takes is painful. He has to walk with a stick. The plaintiff would have problems in walking but particularly on inclines or ladders

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: the ankle is not strong enough to support him when he has to squat over a lavatory basin
the plaintiff cannot return to his work as a painter and would in future be restricted to working as a watchman, shop assistant or car park attendant
